thread:
Sam: Kickoff idea 1: propose a small-scope pilot for a "Guidance Engine" that surfaces batching/caching/quantize recommendations + eval-triggered alerts for customers. Goal: prove value and low friction.
Ivy: +1. What's the absolute minimal output for MVP? A single recommendation card per route?
Sam: Exactly 1 — one card that lists: recommendation type (batch/cache/quant), tier (safe/balanced/aggressive), estimated cost delta, expected quality delta, and a short explanation (1-2 bullets).
Diego: Ops constraints: any recommendation that changes model variant must be reversible via a single-button rollback and produce an audit entry. Also require automated smoke-check after apply (sanity prompts).
Lena: For alerts 1 how are we deciding "eval-triggered"? My suggestion: require both an eval set delta AND production signal change to reduce noise. Example gating: (eval_drop >= 0.04 AND production_concordance_drop >= 0.03) OR (eval_drop >= 0.06). Also require min_traffic threshold (e.g., >200k tokens/day).
Sam: That pattern makes sense. Draft alert config proposal: ```yaml
alerts:
  - name: guidance-regression
    eval_delta_threshold: 0.04
    production_delta_threshold: 0.03
    min_tokens_per_day: 200000
    window_seconds: 86400
    suppress_for: 3600  # cooldown between alerts
```
Ivy: UX note: show "confidence" and "why" link that opens the eval sample where the metric changed. Customers always ask for a repro.
Diego: Pilot acceptance metrics (suggested): 1) two customers complete 2-week pilot; 2) at least one recommendation adopted per customer; 3) measured quality regression rate <= 8% across adopted recs; 4) false positive alert rate <= 12%.
Lena: Add platform SLOs: 99% of rollbacks must complete within 3 minutes, 100% of recommendations must have provenance metadata, and alert delivery < 2 minutes.
Sam: Scope boundaries for MVP: only autoregressive decoder models, single-turn endpoints, recommendations limited to quantization steps and batching/prefix cache hints (no model-architecture swaps). No automated auto-apply for aggressive tier 1 manual apply only.
Ivy: We should include a "preview diff" that shows estimated latency and cost change per 100k tokens. Also include a small simulation run that runs small sample of production prompts through suggested config and shows sample outputs.
Diego: For pilot customers, propose choosing one high-traffic search (QueryHub) and one docs/knowledge base (DocuFind). Both have asked for cost recommendations. I'll coordinate with CS.
Lena: Infra asks: need a sandbox cluster + isolated rollout namespace and a read-only reporting bucket for pilot artifacts. Infra-bot: sandbox created: cluster=guidance-pilot-2026, bucket=gs://redwood-guidance/pilot-1744321000.
Sam: Nice. Next steps: Ivy to draft product one-pager + mockups by Tue EOD; Diego to draft ops rollback/runbook; Lena to confirm infra provisioning + alert plumbing; I'll draft pilot recruitment email. Meeting to lock scope Wed morning.
Ivy: Quick question: any constraints on the eval harness? Which eval metric are we using for quality delta? Sam: Start with concordance and exact-match on our customer prompts; add BLEU-like metrics later.
Diego: Also add a telemetry gate: only propose quantization for routes where 95th percentile latency headroom > 30ms to avoid regressing SLA.
Sam: Good call. I'll add that to the checklist. If everyone OK, I'll open the pilot doc and link to infra bucket.
Infra-bot: pilot artifacts bucket: gs://redwood-guidance/pilot-1744321000/config.yaml, tracker: https://go/pilot-guidance-1744321000
Sam: Thanks all 1 locking this in unless objections by EOD today. :thumbsup:
